title: The window, watched
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Monday. Wood sits in the Datsun across 101 from the frame shop on his day off and counts who stops at the window of empty frames. Eleven people. Four look through a frame. One puts her hand up as if to touch what's in it. Nothing's in it.

panels.composition: 101 from the far shoulder: the frame shop, the window of twelve empty frames, the road between. The Datsun parked on the gravel across.

image.prompt: a low roadside frame shop with a window of empty picture frames seen across a two-lane highway from a parked small car, black and white, no words

panels.composition: A WOMAN at the window, looking through one frame. Her hand coming up toward the glass.

image.prompt: a woman on a sidewalk looking through an empty picture frame in a shop window with her hand raised toward the glass, black and white, no words

panels.composition: WOOD's pad: a tally. Eleven marks. Four circled. One with a hand drawn beside it.

image.prompt: close on a drawing pad with eleven tally marks, four of them circled, and a tiny drawn hand beside one, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Dusk. The OWNER locking the door. Looking across the road at the Datsun. Looking a long time. Getting in her car. Mondays are hers; she let him have this one.

image.prompt: a woman locking a shop door at dusk and looking across a highway at a small parked car for a long moment, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Eleven; four; one with her hand up. 'People will bring their own.' They do.
